summary: Describes a URN namespace for naming persistent resources published by the TV-Anytime Forum, including its standards, XML schemas, namespaces and other documents. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: A TV group wants permanent names for its papers so the links never break. This memo sets up the naming style they will use.

subtitle: A stable naming system for TV specifications and documents.

tldr.problem: The TV-Anytime Forum produces many technical documents and standards, but these resources need permanent, location-independent names that won't break when documents move or servers change.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 4195 establishes a URN (Uniform Resource Name) namespace with the prefix urn:tva: that the forum uses to assign persistent identifiers following a structured format: urn:tva:{category}:{string}.
tldr.outcome: TV-Anytime resources—specifications, XML schemas, and other documents—can now be identified with permanent names that remain valid even if the physical location of the documents changes.

today: RFC 4195 is an Informational RFC describing a URN namespace that the TV-Anytime Forum established for naming its specifications and standards documents. The namespace remains in use today for identifying TV-Anytime resources.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The TV-Anytime Forum develops specifications, working documents, and XML schemas that major standardization bodies—including the European Telecommunication Standardization Institute (ETSI), Digital Video Broadcasting (DVB), the Association of Radio Industries and Businesses (ARIB), and the Advance Television Systems Committee (ATSC)—consider for adoption.

The forum wanted to provide permanent, globally distributed, location-independent names for these resources so they could be reliably referenced across organizations and remain valid over time.
sections.plainLanguage: Different TV groups around the world want to use the same rulebooks. The forum needed a way to give these documents names that work everywhere and never break.

sections.title: The URN Structure
sections.content:
The TV-Anytime Forum URN namespace uses the namespace ID tva, making URNs in the form urn:tva:{category}:{string}. The category is a US-ASCII string following URN syntax requirements, and the string portion identifies the specific resource.

For example, URNs might look like urn:tva:metadata:2002 or urn:tva:metadata:cs:IntentionCS:2002. The category portion is case-insensitive for matching purposes, but the remainder of the identifier is case-sensitive, meaning urn:tva:METADATA:data and urn:tva:metadata:data refer to the same resource but differ only in the case-sensitive portion.
sections.plainLanguage: The naming pattern looks like a postal address: urn:tva: is like the country, then a category like the city, then a specific identifier like a street address.

sections.title: Management and Persistence
sections.content:
The TV-Anytime Forum maintains full control and management of all identifier assignments. Uniqueness is guaranteed as long as each category is never reassigned for different purposes, a responsibility the forum accepts.

The forum commits to maintaining the accessibility and persistence of all resources officially assigned URNs. Persistence depends on proper delegation at the category level and the forum's commitment to maintaining those assignments over time.
sections.plainLanguage: The TV group promises to keep these names working and never reuse a category for something else. That way, old references always find the right thing.

sections.title: Community Benefits
sections.content: The registered namespace benefits implementers in three ways. First, implementers of TV-Anytime specifications can use these URNs to gain interoperability benefits across the broader Internet. Second, developers of other specifications that incorporate TV-Anytime components can use these URNs to maintain some compatibility with the TV-Anytime community while extending the work. Third, implementers of semantically related specifications can use TV-Anytime identifiers—such as classification scheme terms—to enable interoperation with the TV-Anytime implementation communities.
sections.plainLanguage: Having one standard naming system means that software companies building TV systems can talk to each other easily, and other groups can build on TV-Anytime work without conflicts.

sections.title: Security
sections.content: RFC 4195 notes that there are no additional security considerations beyond those normally associated with the use and resolution of URNs in general. The namespace itself does not introduce new security risks; it is simply a naming mechanism.
sections.plainLanguage: This naming system doesn't create any new security problems. It works the same way any permanent name on the internet would.
